title: Compactly supported intersection-cohomology Poincare polynomials of generic GL_n character varieties on punctured complex Riemann surfaces with arbitrary Jordan monodromy
source_title: Intersection cohomology of character varieties for punctured Riemann surfaces
author: Mathieu Ballandras
difficulty_reason: Allowing Mellit and the prior Springer cohomology relation leaves a new geometric obligation before the final matrix inversion applies. Section4 constructs the resolution-to-semisimple diffeomorphism through filtered local systems and parabolic Higgs bundles, including the weighted Sobolev parameter change and its local smoothness. The full construction is retained, so the selected singular intersection-cohomology formula is not admitted merely for formal symmetric-function bookkeeping.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Selected Theorem5.2 over the complex punctured Riemann surface, positive number of punctures and a generic k-tuple in the exact determinant/no-proper-submultiset sense Definition3.2. Arbitrary Jordan types are permitted. This is the Poincare specialization, not the full conjectural mixed Hodge formula. Empty varieties use zero as specified and consecutively proved52–53. New analytic diffeomorphism core4.32–4.33 and all local/global constructions36–50 were read along with the final multiplicity inversion51–53. Named pre-existing Springer/parabolic induction Letellier3.8, Mellit3.13 and Biquard-Boalch analytic moduli/non-Abelian Hodge foundations are preserved as references. The special rank-two four-puncture example is illustrative and is not used by the general analytic proof. All source context retained.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author connects singular character varieties to semisimple ones through parabolic Riemann-Hilbert and non-Abelian Hodge correspondences, proves smoothness of a weighted-Sobolev parameter change and inverts Springer multiplicity matrices. This geometric-analytic construction and intersection cohomology computation exceed qualifying-exam algebraic geometry.
